knownIssues: Side contradiction: the opponents planted and won the pistol round, yet the player is on T.
"All five died" contradicts the "hunt exit kills" qualifier.
"Stack a site" is a CT play but is offered to a T-side player.
"$1,900 is not enough for a rifle" is wrong (a Galil AR costs $1,800).
The reveal says the force buy "broke the opponent loss bonus", but round winners do not have a loss bonus.
A teammate "reporting opponents' buys" is implausible.
The main rubric ranks full_eco highest while the reveal calls the force buy strongest.
Uses a new_information follow-up instead of economy_risk.
Evidence matrix is incomplete (does not cover all action x evidence-pair cells).
Previously labelled "professional" without any provenance; relabelled synthetic.
Economy references are CS:GO-era and need re-checking against current CS2 rules.

brief.title: The second-round gamble
brief.focus: Economy management after losing the pistol round

facts.text: Your team lost the pistol round. The opponents planted and won.
Each player has $1 900 after the loss bonus.
The opponent team has a full buy with SMGs and head armour after winning the pistol.
No one on your team survived — all five died, so no saved weapons.
You are on the T side, round 2.

actions.label: Force buy — everyone buys armour and a Tec-9
Full eco — save everything for round 3
Half buy — armour only, play for picks

qualifiers.label: Playing a default spread and looking for picks
Hunting for exit kills to damage their economy
Stacking a site for a surprise hold
Buying a smoke and flash instead of armour

followup.heading: Teammate intel
followup.stimulus: Your teammate reports that two opponents bought SMGs instead of rifles — likely expecting an eco round from your team.

updates.text: At least two opponents are confirmed to carry SMGs, not rifles.

responses.label: Stick with the original economic plan
Upgrade to a force buy — SMGs are weaker at range
Play passively to punish their expected aggression against an eco

events.action: The team force-bought Tec-9s and armour, then stacked B site.
events.consequence: Two SMG-wielding opponents pushed aggressively into the stacked site and were traded out. The remaining CTs could not retake against the stolen weapons.
events.state: The force buy succeeded, evening the economy and breaking the opponent loss bonus.

comparison.roundAction: Force buy with a site stack to exploit predicted SMG aggression.
comparison.materialInformation: The confirmation that opponents carried SMGs, indicating they expected an eco and planned to push aggressively.
comparison.roundFollowup: Upgrading to a force buy was the strongest response to the SMG intelligence — SMGs lose at range and their carriers push close.

debrief.whyItWorks: SMG carriers play close range and push aggressively because they expect defenceless eco opponents. Armour and Tec-9s at close range rival SMGs, and a stacked site gives the numerical advantage in the engagement.
debrief.cost: If the force buy fails, the team is on a deeper economic deficit — round 3 becomes a second eco, delaying the first full buy to round 4.
debrief.assumption: The opponents will push aggressively rather than hold defensive positions with their SMGs.
debrief.breaksWhen: If the opponents play passively with their SMGs and hold angles, the Tec-9 force buy loses its close-range advantage.

evidenceReview.explanation: SMG buys confirmed the opponents expected an eco — their play style becomes predictable: aggressive pushes for kill reward money.
At the first loss bonus stage, $1 900 is enough for armour and a Tec-9 but not a rifle — the force buy is the maximum available investment.

debrief.followupReview: Upgrading to a force buy after confirming SMGs is the highest-value response. SMG carriers expect unarmoured opponents — armour invalidates their damage model. Saving is safe but wastes the intelligence advantage.
debrief.strongestAlternative: Full eco and save for round 3. Guarantees a full buy next round but sacrifices the opportunity created by the SMG intelligence.

counterfactual.changedFact: If the opponents had bought rifles instead of SMGs.
counterfactual.effect: A force buy becomes much riskier — rifles kill armoured opponents efficiently at all ranges. The full eco into round 3 becomes the clearly safer choice.

debrief.method: Synthetic scenario written for Roundcraft as editorial tactical analysis. It is not a recording or reconstruction of a professional match.

sources.label: Roundcraft editorial analysis
sources.detail: Synthetic scenario; no professional match, team or player is depicted.

reveal.principle: When you have intelligence about the opponent equipment, use it. A force buy that exploits a known vulnerability is stronger than a safe eco that ignores the information.
